summary: An individual intervenor filing as L.M. Marlowe submits a second supplemental technical comment urging FERC to judge show cause responses against physical stability, observability and cost causation, and describing a frequency-response absorption standard evaluated at minimum system inertia.
ask: Hold every framework, tariff and methodology before the Commission to the full requirements of the show cause orders, including physical stability and observability, and consider the described absorption standard.

points.point: Marlowe says a response fixing only commercial access without addressing physical stability and observability does not meet the show cause orders.
points.quote: A submission that resolves the commercial or market-access dimension of large-load integration without demonstrably addressing the physical stability and observability questions that gave rise to these proceedings

points.point: She argues a correlated block of dispersed computational loads could become the largest credible contingency, replacing the largest generator.
points.quote: Where the coordinated-drop magnitude of the block exceeds the loss-of-largest- unit value, the largest credible contingency is no longer a generator

points.point: She proposes testing any behaviorally coupled load block at a credible minimum-inertia condition.
points.quote: the absorption of any behaviorally-coupled load block must be evaluated at a credible minimum-inertia condition

points.point: She says detecting unaccounted-for load and reassigning its cost happen in one settlement calculation.
points.quote: the quantity that identifies unaccounted-for load and the quantity that reassigns its cost are the same quantity.

throughLine.text: Comment filed in the show cause dockets proposing a stability test for large-load interconnection studies, bearing on the operational requirements the June orders ask RTOs to address.
